title: Exclusive Access to Shared Data
goal: Mutate data inside an Rc when ownership is unique or copy-on-write.

sections.text: `Rc<T>` normally provides shared immutable access. You cannot get a `&mut T` directly from an `Rc<T>` because another handle might be reading it.

sections.caption: get_mut returns Some(&mut T) only if count is 1.

sections.text: If there is only one `Rc` pointing to the data, `Rc::get_mut` returns `Some(&mut T)`. If other handles exist, it returns `None` to prevent data mutation under active sharing.
When you need mutable access regardless of handle count, use `Rc::make_mut`. It checks the count and clones the inner data if shared so the current handle gets its own mutable copy.

sections.caption: make_mut clones on write when shared.

sections.text: This technique is called clone-on-write. It avoids cloning when the `Rc` is uniquely owned, paying the clone cost only when sharing actually occurs.

explanation: Mutate data inside an Rc when ownership is unique or copy-on-write.
